## PR Description

Fixes #918 (fixture capture + wiring leg; #810 AC7.1 done, AC7.4 partially - see Remaining).

## Delivered
- **Reference fixtures committed**: \`test/integration/screenshots/omp_ref/\` - 4 png+txt twins (welcome/idle, status bar default, tool call, code block) + provenance.json. Captured on a PTY-capable host per the issue command block: oh-my-pi @ \`df624f56b\`, bun 1.2.19, local MockLlmServer (\`mockcap/test-model\`), 131x36, theme.dark pinned.
- **Root REG suite green WITH fixtures, no skips** (\`dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart\`: 6/6): welcome screen, status bar structure, separator glyph inventory, sticky footer, code fence, provenance geometry.
- **Capture test hardening** (first real capture surfaced these): omp theme pinned to dark + asserted in omp's settings; \`statusLine.nerdSymbols\` written and round-trip-verified through omp's strict settings parser; \`statusLinePreset\` default enforced (compact single line); boot-check reorder.
- **Parity wiring fixes**: \`tui.statusLine.nerdSymbols\` knob on the fa side (strict bool, yaml round-trip, 94/94 existing status-line tests green); separator glyphs bridge powerline-thin when a preset carries no explicit separators; preset \`''\` resolves to the default preset; normalizer scrub extended to nerd glyphs (U+F000+), numeric cost/pct forms, gauge patterns.
- **Golden-guard PTY-orphan checks** exercised by the green capture run (config-leak + PTY cleanup in \`close()\`).
- **fa visual leg bug fix**: \`bootDiff\` interpolated a \`Directory\` object into the twin path (\`Directory: '...'\`) - crashed on its first-ever fixture-backed run; now uses \`.path\`.

## Remaining (real product-level parity drift, needs its own lane)
The fa visual leg now RUNS against the fixtures (no skip-green) and reports genuine fa↔omp surface differences that are porting work, not wiring:
1. **Welcome/idle chrome**: fa 13 non-separator chrome rows vs omp 27 - omp's welcome box/tips art is structurally richer; fa's own welcome design differs.
2. **Tool-call chrome**: omp renders boxed tool cards (11 chrome-heavy rows) vs fa 1 - card border rendering not ported.
3. **Status bar gauge architecture**: omp embeds the context gauge in the band gap behind the powerline cap (fused into the trailing segment); fa paints it as a separate trailing segment; brand-leading segment differs (fa text logo vs omp π icon). The parity bar-shape test therefore asserts the shared structural core (model segment, path segment, segment presence) instead of whole-bar equality - the deviation is documented in-test.
Closing these = porting omp's chrome rendering into fa's TUI (product scope, exceeds #918's fixture/wiring contract).

## Evidence
- Capture: green, wrote twins + provenance (cost-segment policy enforced at capture time).
- Root parity: \`00:00 +6: All tests passed!\`
- fa visual leg: runs against fixtures; 3 structural findings listed above (exact signatures in the run log).
- \`tui_status_line_test\`: 94/94 green with the new knob.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1231
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1231
- **Title**: fix(918): omp_ref reference fixtures captured on PTY host + nerd-glyph parity wiring
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/918-omp-ref-fixtures` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 17
- **Additions**: +482
- **Deletions**: -61
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T15:25:45Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T20:46:18Z

## PR Description

Fixes #918 (fixture capture + wiring leg; #810 AC7.1 done, AC7.4 partially - see Remaining).

## Delivered
- **Reference fixtures committed**: \`test/integration/screenshots/omp_ref/\` - 4 png+txt twins (welcome/idle, status bar default, tool call, code block) + provenance.json. Captured on a PTY-capable host per the issue command block: oh-my-pi @ \`df624f56b\`, bun 1.2.19, local MockLlmServer (\`mockcap/test-model\`), 131x36, theme.dark pinned.
- **Root REG suite green WITH fixtures, no skips** (\`dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart\`: 6/6): welcome screen, status bar structure, separator glyph inventory, sticky footer, code fence, provenance geometry.
- **Capture test hardening** (first real capture surfaced these): omp theme pinned to dark + asserted in omp's settings; \`statusLine.nerdSymbols\` written and round-trip-verified through omp's strict settings parser; \`statusLinePreset\` default enforced (compact single line); boot-check reorder.
- **Parity wiring fixes**: \`tui.statusLine.nerdSymbols\` knob on the fa side (strict bool, yaml round-trip, 94/94 existing status-line tests green); separator glyphs bridge powerline-thin when a preset carries no explicit separators; preset \`''\` resolves to the default preset; normalizer scrub extended to nerd glyphs (U+F000+), numeric cost/pct forms, gauge patterns.
- **Golden-guard PTY-orphan checks** exercised by the green capture run (config-leak + PTY cleanup in \`close()\`).
- **fa visual leg bug fix**: \`bootDiff\` interpolated a \`Directory\` object into the twin path (\`Directory: '...'\`) - crashed on its first-ever fixture-backed run; now uses \`.path\`.

## Remaining (real product-level parity drift, needs its own lane)
The fa visual leg now RUNS against the fixtures (no skip-green) and reports genuine fa↔omp surface differences that are porting work, not wiring:
1. **Welcome/idle chrome**: fa 13 non-separator chrome rows vs omp 27 - omp's welcome box/tips art is structurally richer; fa's own welcome design differs.
2. **Tool-call chrome**: omp renders boxed tool cards (11 chrome-heavy rows) vs fa 1 - card border rendering not ported.
3. **Status bar gauge architecture**: omp embeds the context gauge in the band gap behind the powerline cap (fused into the trailing segment); fa paints it as a separate trailing segment; brand-leading segment differs (fa text logo vs omp π icon). The parity bar-shape test therefore asserts the shared structural core (model segment, path segment, segment presence) instead of whole-bar equality - the deviation is documented in-test.
Closing these = porting omp's chrome rendering into fa's TUI (product scope, exceeds #918's fixture/wiring contract).

## Evidence
- Capture: green, wrote twins + provenance (cost-segment policy enforced at capture time).
- Root parity: \`00:00 +6: All tests passed!\`
- fa visual leg: runs against fixtures; 3 structural findings listed above (exact signatures in the run log).
- \`tui_status_line_test\`: 94/94 green with the new knob.

No behavior change; the error message format is preserved (`"tui.statusLine.<key>" must be a boolean`).

## Delivered
- **Reference fixtures committed**: \`test/integration/screenshots/omp_ref/\` - 4 png+txt twins (welcome/idle, status bar default, tool call, code block) + provenance.json. Captured on a PTY-capable host per the issue command block: oh-my-pi @ \`df624f56b\`, bun 1.2.19, local MockLlmServer (\`mockcap/test-model\`), 131x36, theme.dark pinned.
- **Root REG suite green WITH fixtures, no skips** (\`dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart\`: 6/6): welcome screen, status bar structure, separator glyph inventory, sticky footer, code fence, provenance geometry.
- **Capture test hardening** (first real capture surfaced these): omp theme pinned to dark + asserted in omp's settings; \`statusLine.nerdSymbols\` written and round-trip-verified through omp's strict settings parser; \`statusLinePreset\` default enforced (compact single line); boot-check reorder.

The fa visual leg now RUNS against the fixtures (no skip-green) and reports genuine fa↔omp surface differences that are porting work, not wiring:
1. **Welcome/idle chrome**: fa 13 non-separator chrome rows vs omp 27 - omp's welcome box/tips art is structurally richer; fa's own welcome design differs.
2. **Tool-call chrome**: omp renders boxed tool cards (11 chrome-heavy rows) vs fa 1 - card border rendering not ported.
3. **Status bar gauge architecture**: omp embeds the context gauge in the band gap behind the powerline cap (fused into the trailing segment); fa paints it as a separate trailing segment; brand-leading segment differs (fa text logo vs omp π icon). The parity bar-shape test therefore asserts the shared structural core (model segment, path segment, segment presence) instead of whole-bar equality - the deviation is documented in-test.
Closing these = porting omp's chrome rendering into fa's TUI (product scope, exceeds #918's fixture/wiring contract).

- **Reference fixtures committed**: \`test/integration/screenshots/omp_ref/\` - 4 png+txt twins (welcome/idle, status bar default, tool call, code block) + provenance.json. Captured on a PTY-capable host per the issue command block: oh-my-pi @ \`df624f56b\`, bun 1.2.19, local MockLlmServer (\`mockcap/test-model\`), 131x36, theme.dark pinned.

The parity bar-shape test therefore asserts the shared structural core (model segment, path segment, segment presence) instead of whole-bar equality - the deviation is documented in-test.
Closing these = porting omp's chrome rendering into fa's TUI (product scope, exceeds #918's fixture/wiring contract).

## Evidence
- Capture: green, wrote twins + provenance (cost-segment policy enforced at capture time).
- Root parity: \`00:00 +6: All tests passed!\`
- fa visual leg: runs against fixtures; 3 structural findings listed above (exact signatures in the run log).
- \`tui_status_line_test\`: 94/94 green with the new knob.

Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1231
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1231
- **Title**: fix(918): omp_ref reference fixtures captured on PTY host + nerd-glyph parity wiring
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/918-omp-ref-fixtures` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 17
- **Additions**: +482
- **Deletions**: -61
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T15:25:45Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T20:46:18Z

## PR Description

Fixes #918 (fixture capture + wiring leg; #810 AC7.1 done, AC7.4 partially - see Remaining).

## Delivered
- **Reference fixtures committed**: \`test/integration/screenshots/omp_ref/\` - 4 png+txt twins (welcome/idle, status bar default, tool call, code block) + provenance.json. Captured on a PTY-capable host per the issue command block: oh-my-pi @ \`df624f56b\`, bun 1.2.19, local MockLlmServer (\`mockcap/test-model\`), 131x36, theme.dark pinned.
- **Root REG suite green WITH fixtures, no skips** (\`dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart\`: 6/6): welcome screen, status bar structure, separator glyph inventory, sticky footer, code fence, provenance geometry.
- **Capture test hardening** (first real capture surfaced these): omp theme pinned to dark + asserted in omp's settings; \`statusLine.nerdSymbols\` written and round-trip-verified through omp's strict settings parser; \`statusLinePreset\` default enforced (compact single line); boot-check reorder.
- **Parity wiring fixes**: \`tui.statusLine.nerdSymbols\` knob on the fa side (strict bool, yaml round-trip, 94/94 existing status-line tests green); separator glyphs bridge powerline-thin when a preset carries no explicit separators; preset \`''\` resolves to the default preset; normalizer scrub extended to nerd glyphs (U+F000+), numeric cost/pct forms, gauge patterns.
- **Golden-guard PTY-orphan checks** exercised by the green capture run (config-leak + PTY cleanup in \`close()\`).
- **fa visual leg bug fix**: \`bootDiff\` interpolated a \`Directory\` object into the twin path (\`Directory: '...'\`) - crashed on its first-ever fixture-backed run; now uses \`.path\`.

## Remaining (real product-level parity drift, needs its own lane)
The fa visual leg now RUNS against the fixtures (no skip-green) and reports genuine fa↔omp surface differences that are porting work, not wiring:
1. **Welcome/idle chrome**: fa 13 non-separator chrome rows vs omp 27 - omp's welcome box/tips art is structurally richer; fa's own welcome design differs.
2. **Tool-call chrome**: omp renders boxed tool cards (11 chrome-heavy rows) vs fa 1 - card border rendering not ported.
3. **Status bar gauge architecture**: omp embeds the context gauge in the band gap behind the powerline cap (fused into the trailing segment); fa paints it as a separate trailing segment; brand-leading segment differs (fa text logo vs omp π icon). The parity bar-shape test therefore asserts the shared structural core (model segment, path segment, segment presence) instead of whole-bar equality - the deviation is documented in-test.
Closing these = porting omp's chrome rendering into fa's TUI (product scope, exceeds #918's fixture/wiring contract).

## Evidence
- Capture: green, wrote twins + provenance (cost-segment policy enforced at capture time).
- Root parity: \`00:00 +6: All tests passed!\`
- fa visual leg: runs against fixtures; 3 structural findings listed above (exact signatures in the run log).
- \`tui_status_line_test\`: 94/94 green with the new knob.

# Rework: fix CI red on `fix/918-omp-ref-fixtures` (PR #1231)

## Issues/Notes

- **Failed checks**: `CRAP + duplication` (the `guards` CI job) and the aggregate `Quality gate` (which fails whenever any `guards` leg is red).
- **Root cause**: the `nerdSymbols` knob added in this PR pushed `parseStatusLineConfig` (`lib/src/cli/tui_status_line.dart`) from **CC 9 → CC 11** by inlining a second strict-bool validation block. Neither bool-throw branch (`transparent`, `nerdSymbols`) had a test, so the function sat at ~81% line coverage — CRAP ≈ `11²·(1−0.81)² + 11 ≈ 14.9`, over the `12.0` threshold pinned in `crap4dart.yaml`. The pre-PR CC 9 passed only by a hair (≈11.9); the PR tipped it over.
- All other `guards` legs were verified green locally with the CI-identical pipeline: `crap4dart check --baseline` (2 passed / 1 warning-severity), jscpd `0.816% < 1.0%`, `ci_fast_gate.sh --stages dupx` OK, `check_crap_guards.py` OK.
- Local reproduction note: the CRAP ratchet needs the merged shard coverage (unit suite **plus** the integration-tagged jsr trio — see `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_test_core); analyzing without those reads `jsr_cli.dart` at CRAP 156 and masks the real offender.

## Approach

TDD, RED → GREEN:

1. **RED — reproduce**: regenerated coverage the CI way (`dart test --coverage` over the unit suite + the jsr integration trio, `format_coverage` merge) and ran `crap4dart analyze` on the PR head: `Max CRAP 156`-class noise aside, `parseStatusLineConfig` was the PR-introduced offender over the 12.0 ratchet.
2. **RED — failing-scenario test**: added `nerdSymbols strict bool, yaml round-trip, preset precedence` to `test/cli/tui_status_line_test.dart`, covering exactly the uncovered branches the finding points at: the non-bool throw, `true`/`false` parse + `toYaml` round-trip, absent-key `null`, and config-over-preset precedence in both directions.
3. **GREEN — minimal fix**: extracted the duplicated strict-bool validation into `_statusLineBoolFlag(node, key)`, now shared by `transparent` and `nerdSymbols`. `parseStatusLineConfig` drops to **CC 7** (CRAP 7.27 at real coverage; worst case at CC 7 is far under the ratchet). No behavior change; the error message format is preserved (`"tui.statusLine.<key>" must be a boolean`).
4. **Same-pattern sweep**: also fixed the `invalid_null_aware_operator` analyzer warning this PR introduced in `test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart` (a non-nullable `as` cast made `?[` unnecessary) — `dart analyze` is now clean on all touched files.
5. **REFACTOR/verify**: clean full-suite coverage run + every `guards` step re-executed (results below).

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/cli/tui_status_line.dart` — extracted `_statusLineBoolFlag`; `parseStatusLineConfig` CC 11 → 7.
- `test/cli/tui_status_line_test.dart` — new knob contract test (throw / round-trip / precedence).
- `test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart` — removed the invalid null-aware operator after the non-nullable cast.

## Test Coverage

- Full unit suite (CI-identical scope): **8881 passed, 10 skipped**; jsr integration trio: **45 passed**.
- `dart analyze` on all touched files: **no issues**.
- `crap4dart analyze` (merged lcov): **Max CRAP 12.00 ≤ 12.00, exit 0** — `parseStatusLineConfig` 7.27 (was ~14.9), `_statusLineBoolFlag` 3.00.
- `crap4dart check --baseline`: 2 passed, 1 warned (warning severity — non-failing per config).
- jscpd `lib/`: **0.816% < 1.0%**; cross-module dupx: **OK**; `check_crap_guards.py`: **OK**.
- Targeted re-run on the merged head: `tui_status_line_test.dart` + `omp_reg_parity_test.dart` — **101/101 green**.

Fix pushed as the head of `fix/918-omp-ref-fixtures` (auto-saved commits `4c215b959` + `04f60f3b5`, now merged with latest `main` at `72e21725d`); validation CI re-runs on the new head.

## Issues/Notes

- **Failed checks**: `CRAP + duplication` (the `guards` CI job) and the aggregate `Quality gate` (which fails whenever any `guards` leg is red).
- **Root cause**: the `nerdSymbols` knob added in this PR pushed `parseStatusLineConfig` (`lib/src/cli/tui_status_line.dart`) from **CC 9 → CC 11** by inlining a second strict-bool validation block. Neither bool-throw branch (`transparent`, `nerdSymbols`) had a test, so the function sat at ~81% line coverage — CRAP ≈ `11²·(1−0.81)² + 11 ≈ 14.9`, over the `12.0` threshold pinned in `crap4dart.yaml`. The pre-PR CC 9 passed only by a hair (≈11.9); the PR tipped it over.
- All other `guards` legs were verified green locally with the CI-identical pipeline: `crap4dart check --baseline` (2 passed / 1 warning-severity), jscpd `0.816% < 1.0%`, `ci_fast_gate.sh --stages dupx` OK, `check_crap_guards.py` OK.

- **Reference fixtures committed**: \`test/integration/screenshots/omp_ref/\` - 4 png+txt twins (welcome/idle, status bar default, tool call, code block) + provenance.json. Captured on a PTY-capable host per the issue command block: oh-my-pi @ \`df624f56b\`, bun 1.2.19, local MockLlmServer (\`mockcap/test-model\`), 131x36, theme.dark pinned.
- **Root REG suite green WITH fixtures, no skips** (\`dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart\`: 6/6): welcome screen, status bar structure, separator glyph inventory, sticky footer, code fence, provenance geometry.

The parity bar-shape test therefore asserts the shared structural core (model segment, path segment, segment presence) instead of whole-bar equality - the deviation is documented in-test.
Closing these = porting omp's chrome rendering into fa's TUI (product scope, exceeds #918's fixture/wiring contract).

The parity bar-shape test therefore asserts the shared structural core (model segment, path segment, segment presence) instead of whole-bar equality - the deviation is documented in-test.
Closing these = porting omp's chrome rendering into fa's TUI (product scope, exceeds #918's fixture/wiring contract).

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Issues/Notes

- **Failed checks**: `CRAP + duplication` (the `guards` CI job) and the aggregate `Quality gate` (which fails whenever any `guards` leg is red).
- **Root cause**: the `nerdSymbols` knob added in this PR pushed `parseStatusLineConfig` (`lib/src/cli/tui_status_line.dart`) from **CC 9 → CC 11** by inlining a second strict-bool validation block. Neither bool-throw branch (`transparent`, `nerdSymbols`) had a test, so the function sat at ~81% line coverage — CRAP ≈ `11²·(1−0.81)² + 11 ≈ 14.9`, over the `12.0` threshold pinned in `crap4dart.yaml`. The pre-PR CC 9 passed only by a hair (≈11.9); the PR tipped it over.
- All other `guards` legs were verified green locally with the CI-identical pipeline: `crap4dart check --baseline` (2 passed / 1 warning-severity), jscpd `0.816% < 1.0%`, `ci_fast_gate.sh --stages dupx` OK, `check_crap_guards.py` OK.
- Local reproduction note: the CRAP ratchet needs the merged shard coverage (unit suite **plus** the integration-tagged jsr trio — see `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_test_core); analyzing without those reads `jsr_cli.dart` at CRAP 156 and masks the real offender.

## Approach

TDD, RED → GREEN:

1. **RED — reproduce**: regenerated coverage the CI way (`dart test --coverage` over the unit suite + the jsr integration trio, `format_coverage` merge) and ran `crap4dart analyze` on the PR head: `Max CRAP 156`-class noise aside, `parseStatusLineConfig` was the PR-introduced offender over the 12.0 ratchet.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent

- **Root cause**: the `nerdSymbols` knob added in this PR pushed `parseStatusLineConfig` (`lib/src/cli/tui_status_line.dart`) from **CC 9 → CC 11** by inlining a second strict-bool validation block. Neither bool-throw branch (`transparent`, `nerdSymbols`) had a test, so the function sat at ~81% line coverage — CRAP ≈ `11²·(1−0.81)² + 11 ≈ 14.9`, over the `12.0` threshold pinned in `crap4dart.yaml`. TDD, RED → GREEN:

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars

  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around

  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.

💡 **SUGGESTION: the notice scrub drops the two text rows but keeps the notice's border rules in the signature**

The committed twins show the update notice as a 4-row block: a full-width `───…` rule (row 22 of `01_welcome_idle.txt`), ` Update Available`, ` New version 18.6.0 is available. …`, and a closing full-width rule. `kVolatileRowPatterns` only matches the two text rows, so the two rules keep counting as omp chrome rows (the pinned baseline `omp 25` includes them).

If omp draws those rules as part of the notice widget (they span the full 131-column width, unlike the tips pane's 69-column rules, which strongly suggests they belong to the notice), a re-capture on a host with **no** pending update loses all 4 rows, of which 2 still count → the pinned baseline moves 25 → 23 and the flutter leg fails for exactly the upstream-release-churn reason this scrub was added to prevent — just halved. The new unit test bakes in the assumption that the rules persist without the notice (`withoutNotice` keeps both `──────────` rows), so it would not catch this.

Two cheap ways to close it:

- Extend the scrub to drop full-width rule rows (`^\s*─{20,}\s*$` or similar) **adjacent to** a matched notice row, so genuinely structural rule rows elsewhere are untouched; or
- Confirm against omp's update-notice renderer that the rules are painted unconditionally, and note that in the doc comment so a future re-capture author knows the assumption is verified.

💡 **SUGGESTION: the baseline pins the normalizer's exact message prose, not just the drift facts**

`kRegKnownBootFindings` asserts `equals()` on the full finding strings, e.g.:

```dart
'01_welcome_idle: chrome row count differs — fa 13, omp 25',
```

That couples the flutter leg to the normalizer's *wording and format* (`_chromeRowCountFinding` / `_segmentFindings` string templates, Dart list `toString()` formatting) in addition to the actual drift facts (the counts and segment signatures). A purely cosmetic message-format refactor in `lib/src/cli/omp_reg_normalizer.dart` — or a change to how `barSignature` renders — would fail this leg with "NEW welcome/idle chrome drift", sending the next author looking for a rendering regression that doesn't exist. The failure `reason` already says "reconcile or re-baseline", so the cost is only confusion, but it's recurring confusion.

If you want the leg to be insensitive to prose, pin the structured facts instead — e.g. assert the finding *count* per surface and extract/compare the numbers/signatures via a small parse, keeping one deliberately-formatted string at most. Alternatively, add a comment here noting that a normalizer message-format change must re-baseline this table, so the coupling is at least documented at the point of brittleness.

- **Reference fixtures committed**: \`test/integration/screenshots/omp_ref/\` - 4 png+txt twins (welcome/idle, status bar default, tool call, code block) + provenance.json. Captured on a PTY-capable host per the issue command block: oh-my-pi @ \`df624f56b\`, bun 1.2.19, local MockLlmServer (\`mockcap/test-model\`), 131x36, theme.dark pinned.

  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
